summary: Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (~1885–1888). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1852–1867) and the University of Breslau (~1867–1875).
Heinrich Schliemann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He pursued his studies at the University of Paris (1866–1868) and the University of Rostock (~1869).

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe, later completing his Habilitation there. He served at Zurich from 1841 as Privatdozent, associate professor, and Ordinarius.

Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1862–1866) under Hermann Brockhaus, earning his Dr. phil. He later served as a teacher of classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Jena, Tübingen, and Leipzig, working under Léon Feer, Heinrich August Jäschke, Friedrich Max Müller, and habilitation supervisor Georg von der Gabelentz. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Rudolf von Roth, Siegfried Goldschmidt, Albrecht Weber, Wilhelm Scherer, and Ernst Windisch, holding posts at Berlin, Greifswald, Heidelberg, and Columbia.

Heinrich von Stietencron worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at SOAS, the University of Munich, and Heidelberg University. He served as an assistant at Heidelberg in 1965 and held a chair at the University of Tübingen (1973–1998).

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Ernst Waldschmidt and Erich Frauwallner. He served at Saarland University and Mainz, before holding the Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Heinz Mode was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at Basel, later serving as professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and joined the faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa around 1993.

Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She earned her BA from Vanderbilt and her PhD at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith, subsequently holding appointments at Princeton, Griffith University, and Harvard.

Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She received instruction from traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979 to 1984. She has held a post at Rice University since ~1990.

Helga Uebach was an Indologist and Tibetologist who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1960–1967). In 1964, she took a post as Editorial Consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a linguist who held academic positions at the University of Marburg (~1937–1952) and the University of Cologne (~1952–1973).

Hellmut Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin, completing a doctorate under Otto Franke. He held posts at Frankfurt, Peking University, and the University of Washington, where he held the chair of Sinology (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (1942–1948) and under Paul Debes in 1945. He served as Referent at the University of Hamburg from ~1953 to 1988.

Helmer Smith was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, Richard Pischel, and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He held posts at Lund University and served as professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).
